Before you choose

  • Degree + 3 years of work experience

    Have an undergraduate degree or higher and a cumulative GPA of at least 2.5; the university evaluates recognized accreditation, transcripts and any applicable international-admission requirements. Have at least three equivalent full-time years of work experience within the past ten years.

    University of Phoenix current graduate psychology catalog evidenceUniversity of Phoenix current graduate psychology page evidence

  • Not a psychologist licensing program

    This educational psychology degree does not prepare students for professional psychologist certification or licensure. It must not be treated as an approved clinical, counseling or psychologist licensing pathway.

    University of Phoenix current graduate psychology catalog evidenceUniversity of Phoenix current graduate psychology page evidence

  • Not eligible for federal financial aid

    This exact Master of Science in Psychology Direct Assessment program is not eligible for Title IV federal financial aid. Plan financing for its paid twelve-week terms accordingly.

    University of Phoenix current graduate psychology catalog evidenceUniversity of Phoenix current graduate psychology page evidence

  • State and individual admission apply

    Phoenix offers this exact program online, but published availability varies by state and enrollment demand. The university must evaluate your official degree/GPA/work-experience records and state eligibility before enrollment; a ready course plan is not an admission approval.

    University of Phoenix current graduate psychology catalog evidenceUniversity of Phoenix current graduate psychology page evidence

  • Self-paced within 12-week terms

    Choose two, three or four three-CU courses per twelve-week term, with at most twelve CUs per term and thirty-nine graduate CUs per twelve months. Faculty-supported mastery controls progress within that schedule; the subscription is not unlimited.

    University of Phoenix current graduate psychology page evidenceUniversity of Phoenix current graduate da policies evidenceUniversity of Phoenix current graduate da annual evidence

    Pace used in this example

    • 2–4 completed outside courses per month is a planning assumption, not a provider promise.
    • 6–12 competency units per university 12-week term is a planning assumption.
    • Outside providers are studied one after another in this scenario; overlapping study can change the elapsed time.
    • University loads use unit totals. Prerequisites, whole-course scheduling, start dates, breaks and registration availability can add time.
    • One-time university fees are included once; subtract charges you have already paid.

    What this range leaves out

    • Applicable taxes, repeated-course charges and personal living costs are not included.
    • Applicable sales tax on course subscriptions.
    • Books, supplies, course-specific charges and transcript charges when applicable.
    • Housing, meals, travel, health insurance and other living costs.
    • Rates are before financial aid, military benefits, scholarships, discounts and future price changes.
    • Completed or reported courses are excluded from new course charges; school acceptance of reported credit remains separate.
    • This is a range of known tuition, required university fees and selected outside-course charges, not a complete cost of attendance or a graduation-date promise.
    • The exact university graduate program requires every listed course at Phoenix; no incoming undergraduate or other-program transfer award is priced.
    • The published admission degree, GPA, work-experience and state-availability conditions apply before enrollment.
    • University scheduling, assessment mastery and the capstone completed-credit prerequisite control the actual course sequence.
    • Only two, three or four three-CU courses are scheduled per term; the maximum is twelve CUs per term and thirty-nine graduate CUs in twelve months. This range is three to six paid terms for the full thirty-six-CU plan.
    • This Direct Assessment psychology program does not qualify for Title IV federal financial aid or psychologist licensure.
